title: Section Sign (§): Meaning, History & How to Type It
meta_description: The section sign § (U+00A7) explained: its medieval legal origin, how it's used to cite laws, and how to type it on Windows/Mac.
hero_tagline: What § means, where it came from, and how to type it: click to copy.
intro: The Minecraft behaviour in the edition table follows the Minecraft Wiki's Formatting codes article (read October 28, 2026): the Java chat disconnect, the removal of § from books, the Bedrock fields that display formatting codes, and the Realm-name, player-name and party-chat limits.

editorial_sections.h2: Where the Section Sign Comes From
paragraphs: The section sign descends from the medieval Latin abbreviation signum sectionis ("mark of a section"), commonly shortened by scribes to a doubled letter S. Over centuries of handwriting, the two S shapes were interlocked and stylized into the single glyph we use today.

Its main job has stayed remarkably consistent: marking the start of a distinct, numbered section within a longer legal, religious, or academic text. It remains the standard way to cite a specific part of a statute: "§ 230" is instantly recognizable in US legal writing as a reference to Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act, and the same convention holds across most legal systems that use Latin-alphabet typography.

In Minecraft, § starts a formatting code: § followed by a digit or a letter changes the color or style of the text after it, so §c turns text red, §l makes it bold and §r resets it. Whether the game accepts the § depends on the edition and on the text field you type it into.

Formatting codes are the older of Minecraft's two systems: Java Edition now styles in-game text through JSON text components, which is why a § that disconnects you in chat still works inside a /tellraw command. To try a code in a Bedrock book or sign, copy the § from the top of this page.

faq.q: What does the section sign mean?
faq.a: § marks a specific numbered section within a legal document, statute, or long text: "Section 230" is usually written "§ 230" in legal citation. It's also used more loosely in academic and technical writing to reference a numbered subdivision.

faq.q: How do you type the section sign on Windows or Mac?
faq.a: On Windows, hold Alt and type 0167 on the numeric keypad (Alt+0167). On Mac, press Option+6. In HTML, use the entity § or §.

§ marks a numbered section, typically in legal or statutory citation. ¶ (the pilcrow) marks a paragraph break, most often seen as a formatting-marks indicator in word processors. They serve different structural roles and aren't interchangeable.
